title: Short Stuff: The Mad Trapper of Rat River
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Mad Trapper of Rat River, the unidentified man who arrived near the Rat River in the Northwest Territories in 1931, built a cabin, clashed with Royal Canadian Mounted Police after a trap-line dispute, survived a dynamite attack and a seven-week manhunt (including the first aircraft used in a manhunt), and was finally killed in February 1932. The hosts cover the posse, First Nations trackers, the radio coverage, the 2007 exhumation and DNA genealogy findings (Swedish ancestry, likely Midwestern upbringing), and the mystery that remains unsolved.
topics: first use of aircraft in a manhunt

segments.title: Introduction to the Mad Trapper
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the story of the Mad Trapper of Rat River, an unidentified man who evaded a major Canadian manhunt in 1931 and remains unknown.

segments.name: Arrival at Rat River and first police visits
segments.title: Arrival, trap-line complaint and police visits
segments.summary: Albert Johnson arrived in July 1931 and built a small cabin near the Rat River, near Fort McPherson. After trappers complained in December 1931 that he was disturbing their trap lines, Mounties visited several times, the third visit ending with a shooting and firefight and the fourth with dynamite thrown on the roof. Johnson survived, and the posse withdrew in severe cold and returned to find he had fled.

segments.title: Seven-week manhunt and aircraft search
segments.summary: The manhunt lasted about seven weeks, from December to mid-February, with repeated firefights; Constable Millin was killed. Wop May flew an aircraft over the search, reportedly the first use of an aircraft in a manhunt. The case was also among early news stories broadcast on radio, and Johnson reportedly said nothing throughout.
topics: first use of aircraft in a manhunt

segments.title: Public sympathy and First Nations trackers
segments.summary: During the Depression many of the public rooted for Johnson as an outlaw figure. First Nations trackers were key to the posse following his trail, and one tracker was named Rat. The hosts mention a story that Johnson scaled a near-vertical ice wall to escape a canyon.

segments.title: Final firefight and the mystery of who he was
segments.summary: A First Nations member reported a rifle shot, leading the posse to Johnson's trail and a final firefight in which he was killed. The hosts note that his identity and reason for moving to the remote area remain unknown.

segments.title: Charlie Ratt and the morgue photo
segments.summary: Charlie Ratt helped the Mounties locate Johnson. A photo of his body was circulated in newspapers in Canada and the United States, but no one came forward to identify him, and tips did not pan out.

segments.title: 2007 exhumation and DNA genealogy
segments.summary: Johnson's body was exhumed in 2007 once DNA sampling was viable. Comparisons with more than two dozen families suggested Swedish ancestry linked to descendants of Gustaf Magnuson and Britta Svensdaughter, though no close relatives have come forward. Genome sequencing firm Authrom suggested he likely grew up in the Midwestern United States, based on dental work, scoliosis and isotope analysis.

segments.title: Possible Swedish background and comparison to Somerton Man
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether he could have been a Swedish transplant raised in a Swedish-speaking community. They compare the mystery to the Somerton Man, whose identity was reportedly solved, possibly mentioned in a listener mail.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the short episode, and the outro notes it is a production of iHeartRadio.
